title: Printed-Label Canon Audit -- Attempt Shard
description: One SHARD of a dispatched printed-label-audit judging pass's output (#929), read by printed_label_audit.py --report via a repeatable --attempt PATH. Validates only the shape of what the judge produced -- the untrusted half of this pass. The corpus half (built by --build-corpus, which the judge never writes) is this script's own trusted output and is checked procedurally against its session-held sha256 digest instead, the same trust split canon_harmonisation.py draws between its corpus and its check target. Every semantic binding this shard's verdicts must satisfy against the corpus -- anchor byte-exactness, shard-membership, one-verdict-per-dispatchable-site cardinality -- is enforced in code, never here: a schema can assert this document's own shape but cannot compare it against a sibling file. THE IRON RULE applies to this pass too: a verdict here is a proposal a human reads, never an automatic edit to canon.json or to any draft.

schema_version.description: Format version of this shard file's own shape.

shard_id.description: Which of the corpus's deterministically-packed shards this file answers. --report requires the SET of shard_ids across every --attempt to equal exactly the set --build-corpus declared in the corpus's own 'shards' map -- no shard missing, none extra, none duplicated.

shard_digest.description: The digest --build-corpus computed over this shard's own site_id set and recorded in the corpus's 'shards' map under this shard_id. Copied here by the dispatched pass as a self-consistency stamp -- --report refuses when it does not equal the corpus's own recorded value for this shard_id, exactly the corpus_sha256 binding canon_harmonisation.py already uses for its own attempt artifact.

verdicts.description: One entry per dispatchable site this shard was shown. --report enforces, procedurally against the corpus, that every site named here belongs to THIS shard_id, that no site is answered twice (in this shard or any other), and that every dispatchable site the corpus assigned to this shard is answered exactly once -- none of which a schema can express, since it needs the sibling corpus file to check against.

items.description: One site's judged outcome. THE IRON RULE holds here: this object records that the judge decided a printed label DOES or DOES NOT match a frozen canon target -- never an instruction to act on that decision. `tag` and `label` are carried here (rather than looked up by site_id alone) so --report can refuse a verdict that answers the right site_id but under a label the corpus never printed there -- an invented anchor, exactly as canon_harmonisation.py's own member-triple matching refuses a relabelled row.

site_id.description: The corpus's own site_id for the marked span this verdict answers. Byte-exact; a site_id the corpus never declared is refused as invented.

tag.description: The marked element's tag, byte-exact against the corpus site's own 'tag' -- part of the anchor a matches_frozen_target verdict must reproduce and a no_canon_match verdict must still name correctly.

label.description: The printed payload, byte-exact (NFC) against the corpus site's own 'label' -- part of the anchor both verdict kinds must reproduce.

verdict.description: The closed, two-valued vocabulary #929's plan settles on. 'matches_frozen_target': the printed label re-spells a source term canon.json has already frozen under a different canonical_target_form -- carries the full anchor five-tuple. 'no_canon_match': the judge found no such conflict for this site (which may legitimately have carried zero, one, or several canon rows to consider) -- carries no source_form/canonical_target_form at all, because there is no specific row this verdict is anchoring to.

source_form.description: REQUIRED, and only meaningful, on a matches_frozen_target verdict: the source-language form the judge read as re-spelled by the printed label. Must byte-exactly match one of the corpus site's own canon_rows[].source_form entries -- --report refuses a value the corpus never offered at this site as an invented anchor. FORBIDDEN on no_canon_match: a rejected-referent guess is not the same claim as a match and must not be smuggled in under a different verdict kind.

canonical_target_form.description: REQUIRED, and only meaningful, on a matches_frozen_target verdict: the frozen target canon.json already assigned to source_form. Must byte-exactly match the corpus site's own canon_rows[] entry paired with source_form -- a target the pass invented, or paired with the wrong source_form, is refused. FORBIDDEN on no_canon_match, for the same reason source_form is.
